key_insight: Additively manufactured porous wall lattices can raise hydrogen flashback limits mainly by cooling the incoming mixture near the wall, rather than by strongly changing the overall flow pattern.
engineering_relevance: Wall-integrated lattice structures offer a practical passive design lever for improving hydrogen combustor safety and flashback resistance without major changes to core combustor aerodynamics.
method: Body-centered cubic lattice walls varied by volume fraction and strut diameter
Flow-field imaging and SPOD used to track flashback precursors
evidence_signal: Across Reynolds numbers of 9,000–12,000 and multiple equivalence ratios, the coarsest porous wall configuration showed the strongest flashback resistance, while flow and flame shapes changed only modestly.
watch_item: The benefit appears geometry- and operating-condition dependent, so pressure drop, manufacturability, durability, and scale-up effects need validation before deployment.
paper_title: Effect of Additively Manufactured Wall Lattice Structures on Flashback Limits in a Hydrogen Jet Flame Combustor
